data.gender_notes: Leilah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word ‘laylah’, meaning ‘night’. In biblical texts, Leilah is mentioned in the Old Testament as the name of a woman who was a descendant of Esau, the elder brother of Jacob. Leilah is also used in the New Testament as a symbolic name for the church or the bride of Christ. The name Leilah carries the meaning “Night” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Leilah usually hope their child will grow to embody night and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of the night or the darkness of the soul, representing the transformative power of faith and the journey towards enlightenment.

data.cultural_impact: The Hebrew origin of the name Leilah reinforces its association with the night, a traditional time for prayer and reflection in the Christian faith. Additionally, it highlights the connection between the Hebrew biblical roots and the Christian tradition, reflecting the rich history of spiritual practices and heritage shared between the two.

It also symbolizes the Church or the bride of Christ, reminding us of the spiritual journey we undertake as we seek to deepen our faith and commitment to God. This name encourages us to embrace the darkness of our struggles and doubts, trusting that God is always with us, guiding us through the journey of life.
